item.title: Over half of Android and iOS banking apps have serious security flaws — 2,686 apps across top global banks expose bypassable biometric logins and hardcoded secret keys
item.dc:content:
• More than half of banking apps contain serious security vulnerabilities
  • Hundreds of banking apps contain private keys and exposed access credentials
  • Only 4.9% of banking apps support modern passkey authentication technology

A security assessment covering 2,686 mobile banking applications has uncovered serious weaknesses that could expose customers to financial fraud and account compromise.

The investigation by Ostorlab examined software from 487 banks across 64 countries, covering Android, iOS and Huawei's HarmonyOS operating systems.

Over half of the examined applications contain high or critical security issues, raising concerns about protections surrounding mobile financial transactions.

Biometric authentication and embedded credentials expose security weaknesses

According to Ostorlab, over half (51.5%) of examined applications contain at least one high or critical security finding - representing 1,384 applications, while another 18.4% received at least one critical classification during automated security assessments.

Biometric authentication also presents concerns, particularly among Android applications, where identified weaknesses affect fingerprint and facial recognition.

Their scanner successfully bypassed biometric authentication flows in 35.1% of Android applications examined, despite 73.2% of eligible applications connecting biometric verification to cryptographic keys.

Another concern involves sensitive credentials stored directly inside application packages, potentially exposing data that should remain inaccessible to unauthorized parties.

Ostorlab found private keys, cloud credentials, and software service access tokens in 20.3% of applications, representing 544 banking products.

Google API keys appeared separately in 72.5% of examined applications, although their presence does not automatically indicate compromised credentials.

Such keys commonly support services including Google Maps and Firebase, but inadequate restrictions could allow unauthorized parties to misuse associated cloud resources.

The investigation also identified outdated software components containing publicly documented vulnerabilities, creating additional opportunities for attackers seeking weaknesses within banking applications.

Approximately 41.1% contained at least one vulnerable third-party component, while 18.2% included components carrying critical vulnerabilities.

Weak adoption of modern defenses

Despite the security problems, relatively few banking applications incorporate newer authentication technologies designed to reduce credential theft and unauthorized account access.

Only 4.9% integrated passkey functionality, while 20.2% incorporated application or device attestation mechanisms.

Attestation helps banks establish whether customers are accessing legitimate applications rather than modified copies installed through malicious distribution methods.

However, 79.8% lacked this protection, potentially complicating efforts to identify fraudulent software impersonating genuine banking applications.

Ostorlab also found nearly a quarter (22.3%) of Android applications could recognize remote-control or screen-sharing utilities commonly abused during banking fraud.

Commercial or platform-based application shielding appeared in just 26.9% of Android products examined.

Older operating systems introduce another concern because 99.5% of Android applications supported versions that no longer receive security updates.

Consequently, customers using outdated devices could continue accessing financial services through software environments lacking important manufacturer-issued protections.

Applications from 192 of the 500 banks also appeared on publicly available lists of financial institutions targeted by banking malware.

This represents 38% of the banks studied, although it does not mean their banking applications have been successfully attacked.

Ostorlab emphasized that its findings should not automatically be interpreted as confirmed opportunities for successful attacks.

Rather, it should be treated as “evidence that an issue is present, not proof that it is exploitable in production.”

item.title: I've built dozens of Lego sets — these are the 12 I'd gift this holiday season
item.dc:content:
With dozens of themes to build and hundreds of individual sets to choose from, picking the right Lego set to gift this holiday season isn't easy. Even if you're shopping for someone who's one with the Force, loves vehicles, or wants to expand their floral collection, narrowing down the options can be tricky. But that's where I come in, as TechRadar's resident Lego expert.

I've built dozens upon dozens of Lego sets, have plenty scattered around my home, and regularly cover the latest drops for TechRadar. And throughout 2026, Lego has served up some fantastic new additions to its lineup while keeping plenty of fan favorites around. That includes more sets designed for display, but also plenty that have elements that come to life if you opt to play.

And that's part of what makes Lego such a great gift. Yes, there’s the initial unboxing and seeing what you’ll be building, but there’s also the build process, something you can opt to do individually or, with select sets, use a companion app to build with someone else.

So whether you're shopping for a seasoned builder, someone who's never picked up a Lego brick before, or simply want to surprise and delight someone, I've got you covered. From Star Wars and Technic to Ideas, Art, and Botanicals, I've hand-picked over a dozen Lego sets that I think will deliver a smile and a fantastic building experience this holiday season.

I've built some of these myself, while others I've seen up close; either way, each has something that makes it stand out. And you'll notice a few retailers, including Amazon and Lego direct, based on price and where the sets are in stock.

'Bricktastic' Lego Gift ideas
Lego Botanicals
Rocking Plants 11506

As the sequel to the fantastic Cozy Plants set, the Lego Botanicals Rocking Plants don't just deliver a fun building experience; they can also sit on any surface and provide soothing movement — with a spark of color — with a little push.
Lego Botanicals
Lucky Bamboo

This one is a personal favorite of mine, that I've built and, more importantly, that I gifted. It's the perfect introduction to the Botanicals flowers theme and it's a delightful display piece, as after building, you won't need to water this bamboo to keep its color.
Lego Star Wars
AT-AT

While this isn't the massive 'Ultimate Collector Series' AT-AT, this one is a bit easier to build, with just over 500 pieces, and is a bit more affordable, especially with a discount on Amazon. But this one has a bit more to do with play, as it recreates an iconic scene with Luke Skywalker.
Lego Super Mario
Game Boy

The Lego Game Boy was an instant hit when it dropped last year, and it's aged really well. You'll build basically a one-to-one replica of the iconic portable console, complete with swappable screens for two iconic games. And if you're up for a mod, you can also make this function ... those pieces need to be acquired separately, though.
Lego Star Wars
R2-D2

No Lego gift guide is complete without what's pretty much the most iconic droid from Star Wars. This brick-built R2-D2 has plenty of moving parts and comes with two Minifigures: R2 itself, plus Darth Malak. While this model doesn't make the famous R2 scream, you can rotate the head and move the tools around.
Lego Speed Champions
ightning Mcqueen

Ka-Chow! It took a while, but Lego finally has a buildable Lightning McQueen, and I actually waited outside a Lego store for this set. Right now, to make an even better gift, Amazon's dropped the price from $27.99 to $22.39 for the 270-piece set. This is a great gift for a fan of Cars or Lego's Speed Champions line.
LEGO
Lego Up-Scaled Santa Minifigure 40820 | Christmas Craft for Kids & Adults, Building Toy, Boys & Girls, Ages 10+, Holiday Decoration for Home, 761 Pieces

What's better than a standard Lego Santa Claus Minifigure? An upscaled one, of course, built from 761 bricks and pieces. This larger-than-standard Minifigure will stand over 10 inches tall once complete and will surely be a fun build.
Lego Technic
2022 Ford GT

A bit more advanced than the Speed Champions set above, the Lego Technic Ford GT (2022) features intricate details, and as you push the car forward or backward, you'll see elements move. In fact, the V6 engine inside the 1:12 scale GT you'll build actually has moving pistons. A perfect gift for a fan of cars or the Lego Technic theme.
Lego
Minifigure Factory

If you're after a personalized gift for a Lego fan or simply a fun stocking stuffer, consider the make-your-own Minifigure. You'll want to give this a few weeks to ship, but you can customize nearly everything about this for $11.99, including the head, hair, legs, body, and accessories.

Lego Ideas
Minifigure Vending Machine

Lego Ideas are some of the coolest sets, and the Minifigure Vending Machine is a really neat, interactive one. You won't just build the vending machine here, but also the orbs inside that dispense a random Minifigure as you turn it. You can even customize it further by adding other Minifigures you might have.
LEGO
Lego Art Claude Monet – Bridge Over a Pond of Water Lilies 31220 | Building Sets for Adults, Ages 18+, Hangable Frame for Display, Framed Wall Decor, 3179 Pieces, Gift for Women & Men

From Van Gogh's Sunflowers to the Mona Lisa and Claude Monet's Bridge Over a Pond of Water Lilies, the Lego Art theme has proved popular. And while this isn't the most affordable on this list, the intricate build here is really a labor of love. Once complete, you won't just set it on a shelf; you can actually hang it on a wall. I also love that, true to the Lego Art theme, it adds dimension to the classic work of art.
LEGO
Lego Star Wars Death Star 75419 | Building Sets for Adults, Ages 18+, Collectible Model for Display, 38 Minifigures, 9023 Pieces, Gift for Star Wars Fans

Alright, say what you will about the $1,000 Lego Death Star, but it's a really awesome set that opts for a massive half-circle to display some of the most iconic moments in Star Wars. I mean, really, you're getting a bunch of sets in one. And while it's pricey, this is the ultimate gift for a Lego Star Wars fan.
item.description: From Star Wars and Technic to Ideas and Botanicals, I've picked 12 Lego sets that make fantastic holiday gifts. As TechRadar's resident Lego superfan, I've built dozens of sets, and these are my picks for everyone from first-time builders to seasoned collectors.

item.dc:creator: Jacob Krol
item.dc:description: <p>Jacob Krol is the US Managing Editor for News at TechRadar overseeing the daily rollout of content and coordinating with various section leads. He joined TechRadar in May of 2024 and is based out of New York City. </p><p><br></p><p>Prior to joining TechRadar, Jacob was Senior Editor, Technology and Commerce at TheStreet focusing on covering the latest products in the consumer tech space from how to pre-order to finding the best deals with reviews, analysis, and features in between. Before that, Jacob was a founding member at CNN Underscored, building and growing the electronics section. He also assisted in building out social media channels, programming the homepage, and establishing protocols for testing various products for one-off reviews and best-of guides. Prior to starting at CNN, Jacob was a Tech Writer at Mashable focusing on news, reviews, and evergreen content. </p><p><br></p><p>He has experience covering major players in the space like Apple, Samsung, Google, and Microsoft as well as testing products like smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, smart home gadgets, speakers, earbuds, headphones, TVs, and more futuristic tech like smart glasses.</p><p><br></p><p>Jacob received a Bachelor of Arts in Media & Communication cum laude with a minor in Innovation and Entrepreneurship from Muhlenberg College. During his time on campus, he interned at CNET, Fox News, CNN, and CNBC, while also running his own tech blog, NJTechReviews, which he founded in 2010.</p><p>When not playing with a new gadget or breaking down the latest news, you can find Jacob listening to Bruce Springsteen, posting on TikTok, building a Lego set, watching a Star Wars show, or playing with his family dogs, Georgia and Charlie.</p>
